title: Current-minus-next-year warmth slopes were uncertain for fixed-size moth richness in four British samples in 1992-2014
abstract: We tested whether current-month temperature slopes exceeded next-year same-month slopes for moth catch richness. We used 630 trap-months in England and Scotland in 1992-2002 and 2004-2014. Models controlled trap season, rain, sampling effort and time. All four fixed-size richness contrasts had corrected intervals that included zero. Raw richness had a positive contrast only in later England: 4.03 taxa per degree C, with interval 1.46 to 6.60. Its paired raw-minus-fixed-size contrast was 3.81, with interval 1.48 to 6.13. That paired interval included zero with two-year error clusters. Results do not show a common timing contrast across regions and periods. Shared records, sparse Scottish samples, coarse weather and few clusters limit inference. Fixed catch size cannot separate detection from real abundance change. We test no pollution or causal climate effect. Code, aggregate evidence and a tested raw-source rebuild are included; external records remain outside the baseline package.

display.caption: Current-minus-next-year temperature slopes for raw richness, richness at 100 individuals and their paired difference. Intervals adjust for 12 contrasts and use year clusters. Two-year clusters make the later England paired reduction uncertain.

citations.reason: We adapt its panel-building code and rebuild the same archive. We add current-versus-next-year joint slope contrasts. Biological records overlap.
